messages:
support-team: FYI incoming from customer: sudden tail latency spike in our hosted API after last runtime release, p95 up ~2x, p99 ~3x. Happened ~10:20 UTC. They sent request ids and example traces.
emily: thanks, dropping the request ids here. customer request ids: req_9a1, req_9a2, req_9a7. saw increased queueing on worker pool.
raj: grabbing metrics now. which release tag did we push to that fleet?
tanvi: rollout tag runtime-rel-2026-03-16-4 (not the tiny patch). rolled 20% -> 60% in last 2h.
emily: confirmed. spike aligns with rollout window. p95 jumped from 180ms -> 360ms, p99 from 420ms -> 1.2s on region-us-west-2.
andre: any config changes besides binary? we adjusted batch behavior last cycle iirc.
raj: checking config diffs... hold. I see a change in batching default: batch_wait_cap_ms increased 2 -> 8 in scheduler. also a scheduling priority tweak for short sequences.
tanvi: ah that could increase worst-case for mixed workloads, small requests waiting for batch fill.
emily: repro steps requested from the customer — they run short chat completions (avg seq len 12 tokens) at steady 50qps. they provided a flame trace showing long waiting in scheduler.
ops-bot: automated alert: worker-122 queue_depth spike, avg queue_wait 7.9ms, 95th queue_wait 9.6ms.
raj: can we quickly try toggling batch_wait_cap_ms to 2 on a small subset of the rollout? will need a quick flag roll.
andre: I can push a hotpatch to the runtime config on release group B (20% of traffic) — doing it now. patch command: `kubectl patch deploy runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"batch-wait-ms":"2"}}}}}'`
tanvi: good. also enabling per-route short-seq priority in the scheduler as a temporary mitigation.
emily: after patch, initial signals: p95 on group B dropped to 200ms within 90s. p99 down to ~450ms. customer confirmed a reduction for their sample reqs.
raj: solid. next steps: 1) roll the patch wider, 2) prepare a proper rollback of batching tweak in mainline, 3) add regression test for mixed short/long sequence workloads.
andre: rolling to 60% now. monitoring.
ops-bot: alert cleared for worker-122. queue_wait 95th back to 2.1ms.
emily: I'll coordinate with support to tell customer we identified the batching wait cap as root cause and applied a hotpatch. offering an incident summary.
tanvi: follow-up: add a load test scenario for 50qps short-chat pattern to the canary suite and gate batch_wait changes.
emily: agreed. also adding a dashboard panel to show queue_wait percentiles per release tag.
raj: final note: we should avoid widening batch wait caps without a mixed-workload sim. logging this as post-release action item. closing the thread once we have the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
